subject: Post-call: HealthSys inference evaluation — validation checklist and next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthsys.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: HealthSys inference evaluation — validation checklist and next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the POC scope and compare options (Redwood Dedicated vs hyperscaler reserved GPUs):

Key priorities you called out:
- Consistent 99th percentile latency under 250ms at peak TPS (~80 concurrent sessions)
- Strict data residency in US-East region and audit logs for ingestion/requests
- Clear failover path if reserved capacity is down or degraded (automatic fallback to compatible instance types)
- Predictable monthly unit cost for budgeting

Proposed evaluation slate (2-week initial window):
1) Baseline latency test (realistic workload + synthetic burst) — Redwood hosted small cluster
2) Dedicated run: reserved capacity equivalent (we'll provision a 4-node reserved pool) — measure steady-state and burst behavior
3) Hyperscaler reserved instance comparison: we will provide expected config and run equivalent benchmarks (you may also run on your cloud account if preferred)
4) Failure/fallback test: simulate a node outage and validate automatic routing/fallback and KV cache recovery times
5) Cost model: token-level cost + estimate for reserved commitment vs on-demand/hyperscaler commitments

Attachments: proposed-poc-slate.pdf (high-level schedule) and redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx (initial feature/SLAs matrix).

Open questions for you to confirm:
- Can you confirm whether HealthSys requires an on-prem or VPC private control plane for the test, or is a hosted Dedicated pool in our US-East region acceptable?
- Will you provide a representative prompt set (we can start with the sample set you mentioned)?
- Who should be the technical contact on your side for the trial (for creds, quota, and failover testing)?

Next steps: once you confirm the three bullets above, we'll seed the detailed test-run checklist and proposed dates. I can also draft an initial cost estimate for a 3-month reserved commitment vs a hybrid fallback model.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior SDR, Redwood Inference

Cell: +1 (415) 555-0192

- US-East hosted Dedicated pool is acceptable for the POC. We will escalate to security for a VPC-only requirement if the audit flags it, but let's start hosted Dedicated for speed.
- We'll share a sanitized prompt set by EOD Wed. Example mix: clinical triage prompts (short), longer note-generation prompts (avg 1,200 tokens), and some conversational flows.
- Technical contact: me (Elena) plus my infra lead, Raj Patel (raj.patel@healthsys.com) for credentials and network setup.

Two asks from our side before we start:
1) Can you provide the 99th/95th p99/p95 latency numbers you expect for the dedicated reserved configuration you're proposing? We need these as part of our procurement paperwork.
2) On the hyperscaler side: we are evaluating committed use discounts + reserved instances on one of the major clouds. Can Redwood provide a short comparison table that calls out differences in: guaranteed capacity, eviction/restart behavior, KV cache warm-up expectations, and observable audit log fidelity?

If you can get a short answers doc and updated matrix, we can aim for a March 8 kickoff of the test window.

Sean — forwarding Elena's reply. HealthSys wants p95/p99 expected numbers for the dedicated reserved configuration and a short comparison table vs hyperscaler reserved instances that calls out eviction/restart behavior, KV cache warm-up and audit log fidelity.

Quick notes from our side to include in the response doc: 
- Dedicated reserved pool: propose 4 x A100-q (quantized runtime) serving nodes with autoscale headroom for short bursts; expected p95 ~ 85ms, p99 ~ 210ms at the stated workload (80 concurrent sessions, mixed prompt lengths) after warm-up. Warm-up depends on KV cache priming from the prompt-set; expect 5–12s for first warm requests on long prompts unless we pre-warm via synthetic traffic.
- Hyperscaler reserved instance behavior: capacity is predictable for committed instances, but eviction/replacement behaviors differ by cloud (some clouds will queue, others will evict VMs on host maintenance); cold-start latency and KV cache warm-up will be similar unless you rely on long-lived pinned instances and an application-level cache.
- Audit logs: our hosted Dedicated includes request-level audit logs with request_id mapping and optional exported logs to your SIEM (S3/Cloud Storage). Many hyperscaler-managed endpoints offer similar logs but often with coarser granularity or delayed export unless you install additional agents.

Action for you (Sean): can you draft a 1-page comparison table and a 2-paragraph explanation of how our routing/fallback (model variant fallback + regional fallback) behaves during node failures? Attach to the reply — Elena wants the doc before Fri.

Thanks —
Aditya

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the prompt set. Attached are the two docs we discussed: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx (updated to include eviction behavior and log export latency) and sample-latency-metrics.csv (synthetic run numbers we expect from the proposed 4-node dedicated pool).

Short summary of the deliverables in the attached: 
- Redwood dedicated (4 x A100-qprofile) — expected steady-state: p95 ~ 80–95ms, p99 ~ 195–220ms; cold-start p99 can be higher (up to ~600ms) for long-generation prompts until KV cache warms. We'll include a pre-warm step in the POC plan to reduce cold-starts.
- Hyperscaler reserved equivalent — expected steady-state similar for pure compute, but differences to flag:
  * Guaranteed instance availability vs host maintenance behavior varies by cloud; some providers will migrate VMs transparently, others will require instance replacement (short downtime)
  * Observability: Redwood exports request-level audit logs with sub-second timestamps and optional continuous export; some cloud endpoints only surface aggregated metrics unless you deploy additional logging agents
  * Cost predictability: reserved commitments at hyperscalers can reduce unit cost but often require longer-term financial commitments; Redwood offers a dedicated reservation with clear scale/rollback policies and hybrid fallback to hosted models if you want to avoid full commitment up front

Proposed POC kickoff: March 9 — kick-off call (30m), March 10–23 test window. Let me know if that schedule works and if Raj will need IP allowlist details (we can provide a one-time tokenized ingress for the POC).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx, sample-latency-metrics.csv, proposed-poc-slate.pdf

Best —
